# Design — workflow-bpmn-mechanical-validation

Documentation only. Depends on `workflow-bpmn-diagnostics` having landed: the step this rewrites tells the agent to read something that did not previously exist.

---

## D1. An empty report is evidence; a claimed pass is not

**Decision.** Step 7 instructs the agent to save the file, read the diagnostics for it, quote them, and fix every finding. It explicitly forbids restating the checklist as though it had been walked.

**Rationale.** The two outputs are not comparable. "I checked all eleven items and they pass" is generated by the same model that just wrote the file, from the same reading of it — so if the model misread a gateway's `default`, it misreads it twice and the second misreading is reported as verification. "The Problems panel is empty for this file" is an observation of an independent process.

The old instruction made this worse rather than better. "Report each one, not a summary" was aimed at stopping a one-line "all checks pass", but an eleven-line itemisation of the same self-assessment is more convincing and no more true. Length was the wrong axis.

## D2. Naming the two unverifiable items is the point, not a caveat

**Decision.** §10.7 and §10.10 are named in step 7 and in Outputs, with the reason each is unverifiable.

**Rationale.** Under the old wording these two were items 7 and 10 of eleven, indistinguishable from the nine the model could actually determine. Their honest status — "nothing in the file can answer this" — was lost in the uniformity of the list.

They are also the two with real consequences. §10.10 decides whether a deploy creates a new workflow or overwrites a running one; §10.7 is a case-sensitivity bug that passes deploy and fails at runtime. Separating them out means the user gets a short, explicit answer on both instead of two lines in a list of eleven that all say "pass".

## D3. Annotate §10 rather than split it

**Decision.** `bpmn-rules.md` keeps one numbered list, with each item marked **(checked)** or **(yours)**.

**Rationale.** The numbering is referenced from `SKILL.md`, from the test suite's section headers and from the code comments in `bpmnDiagnostics.ts`. Splitting the list into two would renumber everything and break every one of those references for no gain.

Two items are also annotated with more than a marker. Item 6 says the class rule is a warning **because** the editor cannot see a customer JAR — without that, a user with a JAR reads a permanent warning as a bug. Item 8 splits: the id-versus-file-name half is checked, while whether that id is the `processType` you *intended*, and whether a DCR customization has kept `dataChangeRequestReview`, remain judgements.

The closing note names `reltio.bpmnDiagnosticsSeverity` and states that it cannot demote the hard failures — otherwise the first response to a stubborn error is to turn the setting down.

## D4. No new test script

**Decision.** Rely on the two suites that already cover this.

**Rationale.** `test-workflow-skills-library.cjs` enforces the four-section structure and the reference file's presence — what a documentation change can structurally break. `test-workflow-bpmn-diagnostics.cjs` compares §5's tables against the exported allow-list in both directions, which is the only part of this document whose content a code change can invalidate.

What is left is prose quality, and a test asserting that step 7 contains the word "diagnostics" would pass against wording that says the opposite. Worse, it would create the impression the instruction is verified when only its vocabulary is.

## Test plan

**Automated (existing scripts, no new assertions)**

| # | Assertion | Script |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `SKILL.md` keeps its four H2 sections and its front matter | `test-workflow-skills-library.cjs` |
| 2 | `references/bpmn-rules.md` is present and referenced | `test-workflow-skills-library.cjs` |
| 3 | Every `com.reltio.*` class in `bpmn-rules.md` is in the exported allow-list, and vice versa | `test-workflow-bpmn-diagnostics.cjs` |
| 4 | The bundled skill set is synced at the new version | `test-skills-and-enablement-packs-library.cjs` |

**Manual QA (Tier C)**

| # | Step | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | Ask the agent for a new approval workflow with a deliberate gap (say, no gateway default) | It writes the file, reads the diagnostics, quotes the finding, and fixes it — rather than reporting eleven passes |
| M2 | Ask for one that is correct | It states the report is empty, and separately answers §10.7 and §10.10 |
| M3 | Ask it to copy a live definition | §10.10 is answered explicitly: this deploy creates version N+1 |
| M4 | Open a workspace with the previous bundle | The skills re-sync on the version bump |

## Open questions

1. **Should a command expose diagnostics as text?** The agent currently reads the Problems panel. A `reltio.reportBpmnFindings` command returning them as a string would make the step mechanical rather than merely evidence-based, and would also give the deploy path something to gate on. Deferred with the quick-fix work.
2. **Should the skill refuse to deploy while errors are outstanding?** Tempting, and it belongs with the deploy command rather than with the prose that describes it.
